name: TeamStarWolf - eMudhra Certificate Authority Key Compromise 2026 Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the eMudhra certificate authority key compromise case study. No advisory or root program names ATT&CK ids, so every binding is the study's own. Score 50: the action happened, by researchers and testers (key recovery, certificate forging). Score 25: a capability the primaries name that no one observed (adversary-in-the-middle, code signing). Score 10: a form-only fit (proof-of-concept and self-issued certificates). No technique carries a score for adversary use, because none was observed. Install Root Certificate is left out because it fits only by contrast. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

techniques.comment: Happened, by researchers: the eight P-384 private keys recovered from public certificates by the reporter (2026-10-17 16:27 UTC), by Mozilla (2026-10-17 21:48 UTC) and by multiple people, some publicly (2026-10-20). No adversary observed. Inferred mapping. Sources: [1] [37] [65].

Happened, no malicious use confirmed: certificates forged under the recovered keys, a public demonstration for a google.com subdomain (2026-10-20 12:15 UTC) and the forged certificate Cloudflare saw dated 2026-10-20 18:19 UTC. Partial fit: the technique is framed around authentication certificates. Inferred mapping. Sources: [37] [30] [67].

Capability, not observed: impersonating websites and reading or modifying traffic, as Google (2026-10-20), Mozilla (2026-10-20) and CERT-In (2026-10-21) describe; Cloudflare found no interception (2026-10-30). Inferred mapping. Sources: [3] [2] [34] [30].
Capability, not observed: reading or modifying intercepted traffic (Mozilla, 2026-10-20); Cloudflare found no interception (2026-10-30). Inferred mapping. Sources: [2] [30].
Capability, not observed: two code-signing intermediates, EM OV CS CA - G3B and G3C, trusted by Microsoft (Mozilla bug, 2026-10-18; CERT-In, 2026-10-21). Inferred mapping. Sources: [1] [34].

Capability, not observed: malware could appear signed by a trusted publisher (CERT-In, 2026-10-21); Microsoft blocks the two CAs and NuGet.org rejects them (MSRC, 2026-10-26). Inferred mapping. Sources: [34] [24].
Form only, researchers: proof-of-concept certificates logged to CT on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 (about 107,107 by one commenter's count, Reported). Inferred mapping. Sources: [1] [39].
Form only, testers: origins that set up certificates for themselves under the weak intermediate, seen in Cloudflare's handshake logs (2026-10-21 to 2026-10-30). Inferred mapping. Sources: [30].
